acidity.simpleMeaning: the fresh, sour quality in a drink
acidity.contextMeaning: the sharp freshness that makes wine feel lively
acidity.sentence: Acidity is the fresh, sour feeling that makes your mouth water.

tannin.simpleMeaning: a substance that creates a dry feeling in the mouth
tannin.contextMeaning: the dry, rough feeling often coming from grape skins, seeds, or oak
tannin.sentence: Tannin is the dry, slightly rough feeling, often from grape skins, seeds, and oak.

aroma.simpleMeaning: a smell, especially a pleasant or noticeable one
aroma.contextMeaning: the smell of the wine that gives clues about its style
aroma.sentence: Aroma is what you smell, and it often tells you more than taste alone.

fermentation.simpleMeaning: the process that changes sugar into alcohol
fermentation.contextMeaning: the stage when yeast turns grape sugar into alcohol and new flavour compounds
fermentation.sentence: Fermentation also changes wine a great deal.

yeast.simpleMeaning: a living organism used to make bread or alcohol
yeast.contextMeaning: the tiny organism that turns sugar into alcohol during winemaking
yeast.sentence: Yeast turns sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide, but it also creates aroma compounds and changes texture.

oak.contextMeaning: barrel wood that can add flavour, texture, and oxygen contact to wine
oak.sentence: Oak is not only a flavour like vanilla or toast.

oxygen.simpleMeaning: the gas in air that people and animals breathe
oxygen.contextMeaning: air contact that can slowly change a wine’s flavour and texture
oxygen.sentence: Small amounts of oxygen can soften a wine and change its aroma over time.

lees.simpleMeaning: the dead yeast left after fermentation
lees.contextMeaning: the yeast remains that can make wine feel richer when left in contact with it
lees.sentence: Lees are the dead yeast cells left after fermentation.

malic acid.simpleMeaning: a sharp natural acid found in grapes and apples
malic acid.contextMeaning: the green-apple acid that gives wine a crisp edge
malic acid.sentence: Malic acid is the sharper green-apple acid, the one that can feel very crisp.

lactic acid.contextMeaning: the smoother acid created when malic acid changes during malolactic conversion
lactic acid.sentence: Lactic acid is softer and more milky in feel.

malolactic conversion.simpleMeaning: a change from one acid into a softer one
malolactic conversion.contextMeaning: the winemaking process that turns malic acid into lactic acid and softens the wine
malolactic conversion.sentence: During malolactic conversion, a winemaker lets malic acid change into lactic acid.

ripeness.simpleMeaning: how fully ready fruit is to eat or use
ripeness.contextMeaning: how mature the grapes are when they are picked

body.simpleMeaning: the weight or fullness of a drink in your mouth
body.contextMeaning: how light or heavy the wine feels when you drink it
body.sentence: Body is the weight of the wine in your mouth.

texture.contextMeaning: the smooth, creamy, firm, or rough feel of the wine in the mouth
texture.sentence: Texture is how smooth, creamy, or firm it feels.

balance.simpleMeaning: a good relationship between different parts
balance.contextMeaning: the way acidity, body, aroma, alcohol, and texture work together in a wine
balance.sentence: You are checking how the main parts of the wine work together in balance.
